description: Potential Secret in Instance User Data
rationale: Secret-like content was detected in the EC2 instance user data: an AWS access key ID, a 40-character secret-key-shaped string, a private key, credentials embedded in a URL, a literal value assigned to a password/secret/token setting, or a known third-party token format. User data is not encrypted and can be read by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or from inside the instance through the metadata service. The report shows the detection type, line number and a masked preview only; the user data itself is not stored. Instances whose user data could not be read or decoded are UNKNOWN.
remediation: Remove the credential from user data, rotate it, and load it at boot from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store using the instance role. Replace the launch template/configuration so new instances do not receive the old value.
